subject: App integration bootstrap: SDK samples, timeout defaults & surge plan

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmepay.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@acmepay.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK integration + production cutover windows

Samir — great to hear you’re lining this up. I pulled together a short bootstrap plan and attached sample snippets (Node, Go, Python) and an integration checklist. High level answers up front, then the attachments:

- Endpoint names: no breaking endpoint name changes expected for the standard Redwood API. We expose a stable base URL per region (api.redwood.ai) and a model-specific path. During migration we keep the base and add versioned model paths (e.g., /v1/models/...). We’ll provide a migration mapping file before your cutover.

- Timeouts & retries: recommended client timeouts are 10s for single-call generation requests, 30s for long poll/streaming clients. Use exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503: initial 250ms, factor 2, max 8s, cap attempts to 6. For idempotency, include request_id headers for non-streaming calls.

- Surge handling: configure a graceful degradation path — either lower max tokens or fall back to a smaller model variant. We’ll provide a Canary policy example that steps traffic from 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30-minute windows.

Action items I attached: integration_checklist.pdf and sdk_sample_snippets_v1.zip. Key checklist items: API key handling (rotate before cutover), KMS config if using private deployment, and verifying KV cache warmup for long-running sessions.

Inline Node sample (minimal):

const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function callGeneration(prompt) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/redwood-1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.RW_KEY, 'Idempotency-Key': generateId() },
    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt, max_tokens: 256 }),
    timeout: 10000 // client socket timeout in ms
  });
  if (res.status === 429 || res.status === 503) throw new Error('retryable');
  return res.json();
}

(I put full examples for Go and Python in the zip.)

Let me know a good time this week for a 30-minute SRE sync — Vivek can join to cover runtime and rate-fencing knobs.

—Kimberly
Sr. CSM, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acmepay-integration_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK integration + production cutover windows

Samir / Kimberly — quick technical notes from runtime team: 

- Persistent sessions & KV cache: for latency-sensitive auth flows, we recommend session pinning (same shard) for warm KV cache. If you can, provision a small test pool and run 10-15 concurrent warm sessions to validate 95th pct latency.

- Rate limits: default tenant rate is 1200 requests/min for token-light calls. For bursts, configure client-side token bucket with burst capacity ~20% above average and smoothing over 60s. Server-side we support burst credits for Dedicated customers; if you expect spikes during settlement windows let us know so we can pre-warm capacity.

- Retries: on 429 include the Retry-After if returned. Otherwise apply exponential backoff+jitter. Important: do not retry streaming responses — resume from last saved session id if applicable.

- Observability hooks: add the following headers to your requests to help triage: X-Request-Id, X-Client-Version, X-SRE-Pipeline. We can attach sampling traces to requests if you send us request ids during the window.

I’ve added a short checklist item to the Drive doc for pre-warming and a suggested synthetic test (script included in the zip).

—Vivek
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
